updates.title: Karnataka Government Appoints Effective Date for Karnataka Cine and Cultural Workers (Welfare) Act, 2024
updates.description:
The Labour Department of Karnataka has published a notification bringing all provisions of the Karnataka Cine and Cultural Workers (Welfare) Act, 2024 into force with effect from September 30, 2026.

What changed: All provisions of the Karnataka Cine and Cultural Workers (Welfare) Act, 2024 (Karnataka Act No. 46 of 2024) are notified to come into force from September 30, 2026.

Action: Affected employers, producers, establishments, and cine/cultural workers in Karnataka must ensure compliance with all provisions of the Karnataka Cine and Cultural Workers (Welfare) Act, 2024 starting from September 30, 2026.

updates.title: Karnataka Notifies Final Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2025
updates.description:
The Government of Karnataka has published the final Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2025. The Rules establish framework requirements for registering aggregators and gig workers, managing the social security fund, remitting welfare fees, setting up Internal Dispute Committees, ensuring workplace safety, and filing quarterly returns.

What changed: Following the draft notification issued in June 2025, the Karnataka Government has finalized and brought into force the Platform Based Gig Workers Rules, 2025. Key provisions include mandatory registration of platform aggregators, creation of a digital database and unique IDs for gig workers, remittance of quarterly welfare fees, establishment of an Internal Dispute Committee (IDC) for handling worker grievances, clear deactivation guidelines published in Kannada and English, sector-specific safety standards, and filing quarterly return Form A.

Action: Aggregators must register on the designated state portal, share and map worker database details to issue unique IDs, collect and quarterly deposit the prescribed welfare fee into designated bank accounts, publish transparent terms and deactivation criteria in Kannada and English, establish an Internal Dispute Committee (IDC) with required worker representation, adhere to occupational safety guidelines, and submit quarterly returns under Form A within 30 days from the end of each quarter.

updates.title: Karnataka Labour Department Releases Provisional Seniority Lists for Assistant and Deputy Labour Commissioners
updates.description:
The Labour Department of Karnataka has published provisional seniority lists as of December 31, 2025, for Group-A departmental cadres, specifically Assistant Labour Commissioners and Deputy Labour Commissioners, inviting objections from affected officers within 30 days.

What changed: Provisional seniority lists for Assistant Labour Commissioners and Deputy Labour Commissioners within the Karnataka Labour Department have been published as of December 31, 2025. Officers are granted a 30-day window from the publication date to submit objections regarding entry dates, cadre placement, or personal details.

Action: Affected Assistant Labour Commissioners and Deputy Labour Commissioners must review their details in the provisional seniority lists and submit any objections or representations with supporting documents to the Secretary, Labour Department, Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru, within 30 days.

updates.title: Karnataka Government Designates Authorities under Platform Based Gig Workers Social Security Act and Rules
updates.description:
The Karnataka Labour Department issued a notification designating specific officers as Appellate Authorities, Controlling Authorities, Reviewing Authorities, and Authorized Persons under the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 and Rules, 2025. A subsequent corrigendum was also published correcting the notification date from 24/09/2025 to 24/02/2026.

What changed: Designated Senior Labour Officers as Appellate Authorities under Section 22(7); Assistant Labour Officers as Controlling Authorities under Section 22(10); Deputy Labour Commissioners as Reviewing Authorities under Section 23(3) and Rule 26(1); and Senior Labour Inspectors/Labour Inspectors as Authorized Persons under Rule 11(4). Assigned executive administrative and financial authority for the Board to the Member Secretary/Chief Executive. Issued a corrigendum correcting the notification date to 24/02/2026.

Action: Designated statutory authorities must assume their defined roles for adjudicating claims, handling appeals, reviewing proceedings, and managing administrative and social security welfare operations under the Act and Rules.

updates.title: Karnataka Publishes Draft Code on Social Security (Karnataka) Rules, 2026
updates.description:
The Government of Karnataka has issued the draft Code on Social Security (Karnataka) Rules, 2026 under the Code on Social Security, 2020. The rules lay down framework provisions for the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Board, Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board, ESI Courts, gratuity nominations and claims, maternity benefit complaint processes, and employee compensation procedures.

What changed: Replaces/updates the previously issued 2022 draft rules under the Code on Social Security, 2020. The proposed rules prescribe operational mechanisms for social security boards, procedural guidelines for Employees' Insurance Courts, timelines and forms for gratuity nominations/disbursements, dispute mechanisms for maternity benefit claims, and norms for employee compensation including funeral expenses.

Action: Affected persons and stakeholders may submit objections or suggestions regarding the draft rules to the Secretary to Government, Labour Department, Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru, within 45 days from the date of publication.

updates.title: Karnataka issues draft Industrial Relations (Karnataka) Rules, 2026
updates.description:
The Government of Karnataka has published the draft Industrial Relations (Karnataka) Rules, 2026 under Section 99 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020. The draft rules provide a comprehensive procedural framework for bipartite forums, Trade Union registration and recognition, Standing Orders, notices of change, and dispute resolution mechanisms in the state.

What changed: The draft rules set out detailed procedure for the constitution and function of Works Committees and Grievance Redressal Committees, minimum membership subscriptions and audit standards for Trade Unions, criteria for sole negotiating unions and negotiating councils, rules for adoption and certification of Standing Orders, procedure for giving notice of change in service conditions, and forms for arbitration agreements.

Action: Any person or affected entity wishing to submit objections or suggestions regarding the draft rules must send them in writing to the Secretary to Government, Labour Department, Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru within 45 days from the date of publication in the Official Gazette.

updates.title: Karnataka Issues Draft Rules Under the Code on Wages, 2019
updates.description:
The Labour Department of Karnataka has published the draft Code on Wages (Karnataka) Rules, 2026. The draft sets out the operational procedures for minimum wage calculation, working hours, weekly rest days, dearness allowance revisions, constitution of the State Advisory Board, wage deductions, bonus payment obligations, inspection schemes, and dispute resolution. It also introduces standardized forms for registers and wage slips, and proposes repealing legacy state rules on minimum wages, payment of wages, equal remuneration, and bonus upon final publication.

What changed: The draft rules establish a standardized framework for wage regulation in Karnataka under the central Code on Wages, 2019. Key provisions include a 2,700-calorie intake baseline and family unit norms for minimum wage calculation, an 8-hour normal workday with daily spreadover limits, guidelines for flexible working hours, rules regarding contractor wage and bonus liabilities, and new formats for registers (Forms I & IV) and wage slips (Form V). Upon finalization, these rules will repeal the Minimum Wages (Karnataka) Rules, 1958, Payment of Wages (Karnataka) Rules, 1963, Equal Remuneration (Karnataka) Rules, 1976, and Payment of Bonus (Karnataka) Rules, 1965.

Action: Stakeholders and affected parties may submit written objections or suggestions to the Secretary to Government, Labour Department, Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru, within 45 days from the date of publication in the Official Gazette.

updates.title: Karnataka Publishes Draft Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Rules, 2026
updates.description:
The Labour Department of Karnataka has issued the draft Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Karnataka) Rules, 2026 under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. The draft rules outline regulations for online registration of establishments, mandatory annual health examinations for workers aged 40 and above, reporting of accidents and dangerous occurrences, setup of safety committees, appointment and duties of safety officers, working hours, spread-over, and overtime conditions.

What changed: The Karnataka Government proposed new state-level rules under Sections 133 and 135 of the OSH Code, 2020, replacing previous draft versions. The proposed changes establish electronic registration workflows and fee structures, require appointment letters and experience certificates for workers, set mandatory reporting timelines for workplace accidents/diseases within 12 to 24 hours, define safety officer requirements and safety committee structures, and standardise weekly/daily working hour limits and overtime calculation methods.

Action: Affected persons and stakeholders may submit objections or suggestions on the draft rules to the Secretary to Government, Labour Department, Vikasa Soudha, Bengaluru within 45 days from the date of publication in the Official Gazette.

updates.title: Karnataka Issues Draft Rules Extending Age Eligibility for Private Commercial Transport Drivers Under Social Security Rules
updates.description:
The Government of Karnataka has issued a draft notification proposing to amend Rule 14 of the Karnataka Motor Transport and Other Allied Workers Social Security and Welfare Rules, 2024. The draft amendment raises the maximum age limit to 70 years for private commercial transport drivers (18 to 70 years), while maintaining the age group of 18 to 60 years for other categories of covered workers.

What changed: In Rule 14(1) of the Karnataka Motor Transport and Other Allied Workers Social Security and Welfare Rules, 2024, the eligibility clause is proposed to be amended to explicitly cover private commercial transport drivers in the age group of 18 to 70 years, while keeping other worker categories under clause (f) of section 2 of the Act within the age group of 18 to 60 years.

Action: Any person wishing to submit objections or suggestions regarding the draft rules may send them to the Principal Secretary to Government, Labour Department, Bengaluru, within 30 days from the date of publication in the official Gazette.
